text:
Joel Eriksson Ek is getting the No. 1 center treatment this fall (Hockey Wilderness says it's time to respect him as one, Daily Faceoff says his hot start is legit), and the underlying numbers back the praise more than the scoresheet does. Minnesota takes 59% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, eight points better than without him, against top competition.

What hasn't come is the finishing. Six goals on 11.0 expected is one of the biggest gaps in the league, and that's a gap that usually closes. If you want to know why the Wild's run feels sustainable at forward, it's that their second-line center keeps getting to the net and hasn't been paid for it yet.

The flip side: Evolving-Hockey had his 2025-26 results running ahead of his chances, so last year's line flattered him a bit. This year it's the reverse. Our range has him at 20 to 33 goals.
